<description>
osslsigncode -pass places the key passphrase in the process arguments, so ps can read it.

So instead, pipe it to -readpass -, which reads it from stdin (osslsigncode 2.9+, the Guix codesign manifest uses 2.14). Since printf is a shell builtin, the passphrase does not appear in any process arguments.

Only sh -n was used to verify, not actual signing keys. This focuses on the Windows part of #36651.
</description>

<commits>
cb102c93ef contrib: pass windows codesigning passphrase via stdin

osslsigncode -pass puts the key passphrase in the process arguments,
where ps can read it. Pipe it to -readpass - instead, which reads it
from stdin. printf is a shell builtin, so the passphrase does not
appear in any process arguments.
</commits>

<patch>
diff --git a/contrib/windeploy/detached-sig-create.sh b/contrib/windeploy/detached-sig-create.sh
index fa3095f7be..7ad7c434ee 100755
--- a/contrib/windeploy/detached-sig-create.sh
+++ b/contrib/windeploy/detached-sig-create.sh
@@ -35,7 +35,8 @@ do
     echo Signing "${bin}"
     bin_base="$(realpath --relative-to=${SRCDIR} "${bin}")"
     mkdir -p "$(dirname ${WORKDIR}/"${bin_base}")"
-    "${OSSLSIGNCODE}" sign -certs "${CERTFILE}" -t "${TIMESERVER}" -h sha256 -in "${bin}" -out "${WORKDIR}/${bin_base}" -key "$1" -pass "${cs_key_pass}"
+    # Pass the passphrase on stdin so it does not show up in the process arguments.
+    printf '%s' "${cs_key_pass}" | "${OSSLSIGNCODE}" sign -certs "${CERTFILE}" -t "${TIMESERVER}" -h sha256 -in "${bin}" -out "${WORKDIR}/${bin_base}" -key "$1" -readpass -
     mkdir -p "$(dirname ${OUTSUBDIR}/"${bin_base}")"
     "${OSSLSIGNCODE}" extract-signature -pem -in "${WORKDIR}/${bin_base}" -out "${OUTSUBDIR}/${bin_base}.pem" && rm "${WORKDIR}/${bin_base}"
 done

</patch>
